questions.question_text: A company groups all employees by product line, with each division having its own marketing, finance and production staff. This is:
options: Divisional structure
Network structure
Functional structure
Matrix structure

questions.question_text: A manufacturing firm groups its employees into production, marketing, finance and HR departments. This is:
options: Divisional structure
Functional structure
Virtual structure
Matrix structure

questions.question_text: Which is a disadvantage of the functional structure in a large diversified firm?
options: Departmental conflicts and neglect of product-wise profitability
Specialisation of the employees within their own functions
Efficient use of the resources within each of the functions
Clear lines of authority and accountability for each function

questions.question_text: The main advantage of divisional structure is that:
options: Each division can be held responsible for its profit or loss
Costs are lowest due to avoiding duplication of the resources
Authority is concentrated entirely at the top
Each function is performed by the specialists in one place

questions.question_text: A disadvantage of the divisional structure is:
options: Lack of any focus on particular products or markets
Slow response to changes in the markets served
Duplication of functions and higher costs across divisions
Poor accountability for the performance of each division

questions.question_text: An organisation in which employees report to both a functional head and a project manager has a:
options: Line structure
Matrix structure
Divisional structure
Functional structure

questions.question_text: The main problem of the matrix structure is:
options: Confusion and conflict arising from dual authority
Lack of flexibility in the use of staff
Absence of any specialisation
Too many levels of management

questions.question_text: A formal organisation is one that:
options: Is made up only of the top management
Has no rules and relies on friendships
Arises spontaneously from the social interactions of the employees
Is deliberately created with defined authority, roles and relationships

questions.question_text: The informal organisation arises from:
options: Policies that are framed by the board of the company
The organisation chart that is prepared by the HR department
Social relationships among employees outside the formal chart
Written orders that are issued by the top management

questions.question_text: The "grapevine" is the channel of communication of the:
options: Matrix structure
Divisional structure
Informal organisation
Formal organisation

questions.question_text: An advantage of the informal organisation to the management is that it:
options: Removes the need for any formal communication channels
Prevents the spread of rumours among the employees
Meets social needs and gives quick feedback
Has a clearly defined chart of authority and duties

questions.question_text: Delegation of authority means:
options: Assigning the authority and responsibility for tasks to a subordinate
Handing over all the responsibility to the subordinate and relieving oneself
Keeping all the decision-making power with the manager
Taking back the authority already given to subordinates

questions.question_text: The three elements of delegation are:
options: Planning, organising and controlling
Delegation, decentralisation and centralisation
Authority, responsibility and accountability
Authority, power and influence

questions.question_text: Which of the following CANNOT be delegated?
options: Accountability
Responsibility for performing a task
Right to decide on routine matters
Authority

questions.question_text: The process of dividing a task, giving authority and creating accountability is known as:
options: Delegation
Departmentation
Decentralisation
Coordination

questions.question_text: Authority flows:
options: Upwards, from subordinate to superior
Downwards, from superior to subordinate
Sideways, between the peers
In both directions with no pattern

questions.question_text: Responsibility flows:
options: Sideways, since the peers share it among themselves
Upwards, since the subordinate answers to the superior
Downwards, since the superior assigns it to the subordinate
Outwards, since it is owed to the customers of the firm

questions.question_text: Decentralisation differs from delegation in that decentralisation is:
options: The act of taking back authority from the lower levels
A temporary arrangement between a manager and one subordinate
A systematic dispersal of authority throughout the organisation as a policy
Done only for the benefit of top management

questions.question_text: An advantage of decentralisation is:
options: Closer control by the top management over every detail
Uniformity in all the decisions taken by the organisation
Easier coordination between the various units of the firm
Quicker decisions at lower levels and growth of managerial talent

questions.question_text: Which among these is a limitation of decentralisation?
options: Delay in decision making at the lower levels
Difficulty in maintaining uniformity and coordination
Lack of motivation among the lower-level managers
Overburdening of the top management

questions.question_text: Centralisation is suitable when:
options: The firm is large and operates in many areas
Decisions are to be made on local conditions
The managers at the lower levels are highly skilled
The firm is small, and quick uniform action is needed

questions.question_text: Span of management refers to:
options: The time within which a manager must complete the task
The number of subordinates who report directly to one manager
The area covered by the activities of a firm
The number of levels in the hierarchy of the organisation

questions.question_text: A narrow span of management results in:
options: A matrix structure with dual reporting
A tall structure with many levels of management
A decentralised structure with fewer managers
A flat structure with fewer levels

questions.question_text: A wide span of control is likely to be effective when:
options: The managers are inexperienced in their jobs
The work involves frequent changes and risks
Subordinates are highly trained and the work is routine
Subordinates are untrained and the work is complex

questions.question_text: A flat organisation is characterised by:
options: Strict chain of command with specialised functions
Many levels and narrow span of management
Heavy reliance on the formal rules and procedures
Few levels and wide span of management

questions.question_text: A disadvantage of tall structures is:
options: Closer supervision of the employees by their managers
Greater opportunities for promotion of the employees
Narrow span of management at every level of the firm
Slow communication and the higher cost of management

questions.question_text: Line authority is the authority that:
options: Is exercised by the board of directors of the company alone
Is shared equally between two managers of the same rank
Is given to specialists in order to advise the line managers
Flows from superior to subordinate along the chain of command

questions.question_text: Staff authority refers to:
options: The right to advise and assist the line managers
The right to take final decisions on the policy matters
The right to recruit employees for the line departments
The right to give orders to the subordinate in the chain

questions.question_text: The HR manager advising the production manager on a recruitment issue is exercising:
options: Functional authority
Line authority
Delegated authority
Staff authority

questions.question_text: Functional authority is the right of a specialist to:
options: Take decisions on all matters of a department
Advise the line managers when asked to do so
Supervise the work of the workers in a department
Issue orders on a particular function across the departments
questions.explanation: Limited command over a specific function.

questions.question_text: The finance manager issues instructions on budgeting to all departments. He exercises:
options: Staff authority
Informal authority
Functional authority
Line authority

questions.question_text: The chain of command is violated when:
options: A subordinate receives orders from two superiors
A subordinate reports to his immediate superior
A manager delegates a task to the subordinate
The superior guides the subordinate on a task

questions.question_text: An organisation chart shows:
options: The informal groups that exist within the organisation
The market position of the organisation
The financial position of the organisation
The formal relationships among the positions in the organisation

questions.question_text: Departmentation is the process of:
options: Dividing the work among the employees of a department
Appointing the heads of the departments in the firm
Assigning the budget to each of the departments
Grouping activities into units for the purpose of management

questions.question_text: Grouping by territory or area is known as:
options: Product departmentation
Customer departmentation
Functional departmentation
Geographic departmentation

questions.question_text: A bank with separate branches for retail customers and corporate customers uses:
options: Customer departmentation
Process departmentation
Product departmentation
Geographic departmentation

questions.question_text: A textile factory has separate departments for spinning, weaving and dyeing. This is:
options: Functional departmentation
Territorial departmentation
Process departmentation
Customer departmentation

questions.question_text: The first step in the process of organising is:
options: Establishing reporting relationships
Departmentation
Identification and division of work
Assignment of duties

questions.question_text: A benefit of organising is:
options: Clarity of working relationships and optimum use of resources
Increased conflict between the departments of the firm
Reduced clarity of the roles of the employees of the firm
Duplication of the efforts of the employees of the firm

questions.question_text: Organising is a process that:
options: Motivates the employees to work towards the objectives
Compares the actual performance with the standards set
Selects the right persons for the right jobs in the firm
Brings the human and material resources together for the objectives

questions.question_text: A bureaucratic organisation, according to Max Weber, is marked by:
options: Flexibility, informality and personal loyalty to the leader
Absence of written rules, procedures and records
Frequent rotation of jobs among all the employees
Rules, hierarchy, specialisation and impersonal relations

questions.question_text: A virtual organisation is one that:
options: Operates only through physical offices and its own staff
Employs all its workers on a permanent basis only
Uses networks and outsourcing in place of a large physical set-up
Has no customers or suppliers with which it deals

questions.question_text: A boundaryless organisation tries to:
options: Increase the number of levels in the hierarchy of the firm
Limit all communication to the formal channels of the firm
Remove the barriers between departments, levels and outsiders
Strengthen the vertical chain of command in the firm

questions.question_text: A team-based structure is one in which:
options: Empowered teams carry out the work and answer for the results
Authority is centralised at the top of the organisation
Individuals work alone under the strict supervision of managers
Teams are formed only by the top managers of the firm

questions.question_text: A learning organisation is one that:
options: Takes no interest in the feedback of the firm's customers
Continuously gains and shares knowledge and changes behaviour
Trains the employees only once at the time of their joining
Relies on fixed procedures and avoids any kind of change

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of mechanistic organisation?
options: Low formalisation and wide span of control
Open networks and spontaneous teams
Flexible roles, open communication and decentralised decisions
Rigid hierarchy, clear rules and centralised decision making

questions.question_text: An organic structure is more suitable for:
options: A stable and predictable environment
A dynamic and unpredictable environment
A firm with routine operations
A firm with a strict hierarchy

questions.question_text: Burns and Stalker distinguished between:
options: Centralised and decentralised
Line and staff
Formal and informal groups
Mechanistic and organic systems

questions.question_text: Under the contingency approach, the design of an organisation depends mainly on:
options: The personal preference of the founder of the firm
The size of the board of directors of the firm
The number of the employees working in the firm
The environment and the strategy of the firm

questions.question_text: A limitation of the organisation chart is that it:
options: Shows the line of command in the form of a chart
Shows the levels of management in the organisation
Does not show informal relations and the actual authority
Shows the formal relationships among the positions only

questions.question_text: A manager gives her subordinate the authority to approve expenses up to Rs 10,000. This is:
options: Delegation of authority
Abdication of authority
Informal authority
Centralisation of authority

questions.question_text: If a manager gives a task to a subordinate but gives no authority, the likely result is:
options: The subordinate cannot perform effectively
The subordinate will perform better
The authority will be taken by the peers
The manager is relieved of responsibility

questions.question_text: Authority without responsibility leads to:
options: Lack of control
Wasted resources
Better performance
Misuse of power

questions.question_text: Responsibility without authority results in:
options: Increased power for the subordinate concerned
Misuse of the authority by the subordinate concerned
Greater control for the superior over the subordinate
Frustration and inability to achieve the results

questions.question_text: The principle of "parity of authority and responsibility" means:
options: Authority should be more than responsibility
Authority and responsibility are unrelated
Authority should be equal to the responsibility
Responsibility should be more than authority

questions.question_text: A barrier to effective delegation is:
options: The manager's fear of losing control or doubt on competence
Clear definition of the tasks that are to be delegated
Proper training that is given to the subordinates
Proper controls that are established by the manager

questions.question_text: The principle of management by exception is useful for:
options: Centralising all the decisions of the firm at the top level
Eliminating the need for any kind of control in the firm
Reducing the span of management at every level of the firm
Delegation, since the manager handles only the unusual matters

questions.question_text: An organisation which has a high level of formalisation will:
options: Have a flat structure
Rely on informal understanding among the employees
Have flexible job roles
Have written rules, procedures and job descriptions

questions.question_text: A "job description" outlines:
options: The performance appraisal of the employee
The salary and benefits of the employee
The duties and responsibilities of a position
The qualifications required of the person holding the job

questions.question_text: A job specification outlines:
options: The duties and tasks which are to be performed on the job
The salary and the benefits that are paid for the job
The qualifications and skills required of the job holder
The reporting relationships of the job in the organisation

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a basis of departmentation?
options: Product
Function
Territory
Salary

questions.question_text: The manager can use the informal organisation to:
options: Remove the need for the chain of command in the firm
Replace the formal organisation of the firm completely
Eliminate the grapevine from the organisation altogether
Understand employee concerns and speed up communication

questions.question_text: A limitation of informal organisation is:
options: Spread of rumours and resistance to change
Fulfilment of the social needs of the employees
Quick feedback to the management
Reduction of the load on the managers

questions.question_text: The sphere within which a superior can control the activities of subordinates in a firm is called:
options: Span of management
Scalar chain
Departmentation
Line authority

questions.question_text: In a firm of 1000 employees with a span of 10 at each level, how many levels of management are there (beyond the top)?
options: 10 levels
3 levels
4 levels
2 levels

questions.question_text: If the span is increased from 5 to 10 for a 100-person unit, the number of supervisors needed:
options: Falls from 20 to 10
Falls from 100 to 50
Remains at 20
Rises from 10 to 20

questions.question_text: When authority is centralised, the decision making is:
options: Concentrated at the top
Left to the workers
Shared with the customers
Spread throughout the organisation

questions.question_text: Which statement is true about decentralisation?
options: It is merely a transfer of work between two employees
It is a philosophy that reflects the policy of the management
It can be done in any way that individual managers wish
It is the same as delegation for one specific task

questions.question_text: Responsibility is the obligation of a subordinate to:
options: Delegate the work to others
Perform the duty assigned to him
Create the policies
Give orders to the superior

questions.question_text: Accountability means:
options: Planning the work
Distributing the authority
Being answerable for the final outcome
Giving orders to the subordinates

questions.question_text: The BEST example of organising is a manager who:
options: Groups tasks into jobs and assigns them to employees
Motivates the employees to put in extra effort at work
Sets the targets of the unit for the next financial year
Compares the actual sales with the targets set earlier

questions.question_text: A principle of organising which says a person should report to one boss is:
options: Delegation
Unity of command
Span of control
Departmentation

questions.question_text: The most common cause of conflict in a matrix organisation is:
options: Dual reporting of employees
Single reporting line
Lack of specialists
Rigid hierarchy

questions.question_text: The geographic structure is likely to be adopted by:
options: A company with a small number of employees
A company serving customers in widely spread regions
A company with a single product line only
A company with a single factory and one market

questions.question_text: A firm's emphasis on empowerment implies:
options: Centralising the decision making at the top level
Reducing the responsibility of the employees at work
Giving the employees more authority to make decisions
Increasing the supervision over the employees at work

questions.question_text: Which type of structure leads to the most specialisation of the employees?
options: Team structure
Matrix structure
Divisional structure
Functional structure

questions.question_text: The line and staff organisation combines:
options: Only the line managers working in the various departments
Two bosses for each employee in the organisation
The command of line managers with the expertise of specialists
Only the specialists working in the various departments

questions.question_text: In a hospital, the doctors advise the administration on health matters. The doctors have:
options: Line authority
Centralised authority
Staff authority
Delegated authority

questions.question_text: Staff positions are created to:
options: Reduce the span of management at every level
Advise and support line managers in specialised matters
Replace the line managers in the chain of command
Take over the line responsibilities of the managers

questions.question_text: The relationship between authority and power is that:
options: Authority is the legitimate right to command whereas power is the ability to influence
Both are unrelated
Both are the same thing
Authority is the ability to influence whereas power is the legal right

questions.question_text: Which of these is a source of informal power?
options: Designation
Position in the hierarchy
Legal sanction
Personal expertise

questions.question_text: When the top management gives lower levels more freedom in decision making, there is an increase in:
options: Decentralisation
Centralisation
Span of control
Formalisation

questions.question_text: Which factor increases the degree of decentralisation?
options: Larger size and wider geographical spread of the firm
Lack of capable subordinates in the lower levels
The need for a uniform policy throughout the firm
Higher cost of the decisions to be taken in the firm

questions.question_text: Which of these tends to favour centralisation?
options: Capable lower-level managers
The need for uniformity and control
Need for quick local decisions
Wide geographical spread of the firm

questions.question_text: The principle of "scalar chain" is the basis for:
options: The measure of the span of management
The hierarchy of authority in an organisation
The division of work between the specialists
The grouping of the activities by function

questions.question_text: The "unity of direction" principle requires:
options: One boss for each subordinate in the firm
One plan and one head for a group of activities with one aim
One level of authority for each manager in the firm
One department for every function in the firm

questions.question_text: The functional organisation is also known as:
options: Weber's bureaucracy
Fayol's scalar chain
Taylor's functional foremanship
Mayo's human relations

questions.question_text: A drawback of the line organisation is:
options: Delay in coordination between the departments
Divided loyalty on the part of the employees
Overloading of line managers and lack of specialists
Lack of clarity in the authority of the managers

questions.question_text: Which structure has the shortest decision path in a small business?
options: Matrix structure
Network structure
Simple line structure
Divisional structure

questions.question_text: Delegation helps a manager by increasing:
options: Authority over all the details of the work
Capacity to take on more work and to develop subordinates
Responsibility for the tasks of the subordinates
Workload with the routine tasks of the department

questions.question_text: An organisation's ability to respond to its environment depends mainly on its:
options: Structure, which determines how flexible it is
Name chosen for the firm by its promoters
Choice of the colour of its logo and stationery
Location of its head office in a city

questions.question_text: "Organisation" in the sense of structure refers to:
options: The process of recruiting the employees for the firm
The total of the profits earned by the firm in a year
The framework within which managerial and operative tasks are done
The relationship of the firm with its customers

questions.question_text: "Organising" as a process refers to:
options: The names of the departments
Identification of activities, grouping them and assigning authority
The final structure of a firm
The framework of authority-responsibility relationships

questions.question_text: The amount of authority delegated depends on:
options: The colour of the files in which the papers are kept
The nature of the task, competence of the subordinate and controls
The size of the office building in which the firm works
The age of the manager who has to delegate the authority

questions.question_text: An example of coordination through a structure is:
options: The logo of the company
The salary slips of the employees
Individual targets for each worker
Regular meetings between department heads

questions.question_text: A committee is a group of persons who:
options: Audit the accounts of the firm at the year end
Meet to discuss and decide on matters assigned to them
Are the creditors of the firm and lend it money
Are the owners of the firm and hold its capital

questions.question_text: A standing committee is:
options: A committee of the shareholders
A committee which has no powers
A permanent committee with a continuing responsibility
A temporary committee formed for one purpose

questions.question_text: An ad hoc committee is:
options: A committee that is made up of the staff of the firm
A temporary committee set up for a specific purpose
A committee that handles the routine matters of the firm
A permanent committee which functions all the time

questions.question_text: An advantage of a committee is:
options: Lower cost than the individual decision making
Pooling of knowledge and group decision making
Accountability resting on a single person
Quicker decisions than the single manager's

questions.question_text: A disadvantage of a committee is:
options: Lack of different views in the decisions
Time consumption and diffused accountability
Absence of any coordination in the decisions
Dependence of the decisions on a single person
